title: Medical vs Recreational Weed: What's the Difference?
h1: Shopping as a Medical Patient or an Adult-Use Customer in Michigan
metaDescription: Medical vs recreational weed in Michigan: who qualifies, age and ID rules, taxes, purchase limits, whether products differ and how checkout works for each.
excerpt: One plant, two rulebooks. See how Michigan's medical and adult-use paths compare on age, ID, taxes, limits and checkout.
keyTakeaways: Medical and adult-use cannabis come from the same plants; the rules differ on who can buy, the taxes and the limits.
Adult-use shoppers must be 21 and show photo ID; registered patients 18 and up bring their registry card and a photo ID.
Registered patients skip Michigan's 10% excise tax and pay just the 6% sales tax; adult-use buyers pay both.
Patients can purchase as much as 2.5 ounces daily, with a monthly ceiling of 10 ounces; adult-use buyers can get up to 2.5 ounces per transaction.
A card means a $40 state fee every two years plus a physician's certification; it matters most to frequent buyers, and it's the only legal route for patients aged 18 to 20.
body:
Medical vs recreational weed in Michigan is mostly a question of rules, not plants. Patients and adult-use customers both buy tested, labeled cannabis from licensed stores, but they differ on age, ID, taxes and purchase limits. Here's how the two paths compare as of October 2026, and what checkout looks like for each.

## Medical vs recreational weed: one plant, two rulebooks

Medical cannabis isn't a separate plant. One state agency, the Cannabis Regulatory Agency (CRA), licenses and oversees medical and adult-use businesses alike. Whichever path you buy under, Michigan requires every product to be sealed and labeled with its THC and CBD levels, the lab that tested it and a set of warnings. What changes is the legal path, and that path sets your age requirement, your taxes and your limits.

## Who each path is for: registered patients and adults 21+

**Adult-use customers** are adults 21 or older. Michigan's 2018 voter-approved law covers people 21 and up, and nobody younger.

**Medical patients** are people registered with Michigan's medical marijuana program, which is open only to Michigan residents. Patients 18 and older can apply for themselves, and every application needs a certification from a Michigan-licensed physician. Michigan law also honors a valid, unexpired medical card from another state, shown with a photo ID, at licensed medical provisioning centers; if that's you, ask your store before you go.

High Society welcomes both kinds of shoppers: adults 21 and up buying for adult use, and card-carrying patients 18 and up.

## Age, ID and card requirements at the counter

- **Adult-use:** bring a valid government photo ID that proves you're 21 or older; at High Society, a passport also works. Michigan stores check ID before every sale.
- **Medical:** bring your registry card and a photo ID, like a driver's license, every time you buy. A physician's form or a pending application doesn't count as a card.
- **Patients 18 to 20:** adult-use sales start at 21, so a valid medical card is the one legal way to buy at that age.

## Taxes and total cost side by side

| | Adult-use | Registered patient |
|---|---|---|
| 10% excise tax | Yes | No |
| 6% sales tax | Yes, figured on the price plus the excise | Yes |
| Tax on $100 of cannabis | $16.60 | $6.00 |
| What you pay | $116.60 | $106.00 |

Over a year of regular shopping, that gap adds up. A card brings its own costs, though: a $40 state fee for a card that lasts two years, plus the physician's visit. At these tax rates, the savings repay the $40 fee once you've spent roughly $380 during the card's two-year life, before you count the doctor's visit. Shelf prices are set by each store and change often, so check the menu.

## Purchase and possession limits

| | Adult-use (21+) | Registered patient |
|---|---|---|
| Buying | Up to 2.5 oz in one transaction, 15 g of it concentrate at most | Up to 2.5 oz per day and 10 oz per month |
| Carrying | Up to 2.5 oz, with no more than 15 g as concentrate | Up to 2.5 oz of usable marijuana; infused products count by a set equivalency |
| Growing at home | Up to 12 plants | Up to 12 plants, unless a caregiver grows for you |

At home, adults 21 and older may store as much as 10 ounces, along with whatever their own plants yield, provided any amount over 2.5 ounces is under lock. For the rest of the state's rules, see our [Michigan cannabis law page](/cannabis-laws-by-state/michigan/).

## Do medical products differ? Potency, formats and labels

For the most part, no. Flower, vapes and concentrates come from the same plants on both sides of the counter. Every product sold in Michigan carries a label showing its THC and CBD levels and the lab that tested it. Medical flower isn't stronger by default. The real differences show up in infused products:

- **Edibles:** adult-use edibles are limited to 10 mg of THC a serving, while medical edibles may contain as much as 50 mg. Both are capped at 200 mg per package.
- **Tinctures and capsules:** adult-use products top out at 10 mg per dose; medical products can go as high as 100 mg per dose.

What a given store offers depends on its licenses and its menu, so ask your store what's available to you as a patient.

## Legal protections and practical trade-offs: card fees and renewals

- **Protection:** under Michigan's medical law, a patient's protection from arrest depends on showing police a valid registry card plus photo ID.
- **Cost:** $40 to the state every two years, plus whatever the physician's certification costs.
- **Renewals:** cards last two years, and a renewal can go in as early as 90 days before yours expires. Our page on [how to apply for a Michigan card](/getting-a-medical-card/) walks through the steps.

For a fuller look at whether a card makes sense for you, read our breakdown of [Michigan medical card benefits](/blog/michigan-medical-marijuana-card-benefits/).

## Deciding which path fits you

- **Patients 18 to 20:** a valid medical card is the only way to buy legally.
- **Adults 21+ who buy now and then:** adult-use is usually simplest; bring your ID and shop.
- **Adults 21+ who buy often:** if a physician certifies you for the program, weigh the roughly 10.6% tax difference against the $40 fee and the doctor's visit.
- **Patients comparing infused products:** per-serving limits on medical edibles, tinctures and capsules are higher than adult-use limits.
- **Not sure whether you qualify?** That's a question for a physician. Our [patient guide](/patient-guide/) covers shopping as a patient, and our [FAQ](/faq/) answers common questions.

When you're ready, [find a High Society store near you](/dispensary-locations/) and bring the right ID.

Recreational shopping is available to individuals 21 years or older. Individuals 18 and older with a medical marijuana card can also make purchases.

faq.q: Is medical marijuana stronger than recreational?
faq.a: Not by nature. Medical and adult-use flower, vapes and concentrates come from the same plants, and every product sold in Michigan is labeled with its THC and CBD levels. The difference is in infused products: medical edibles are allowed up to 50 mg of THC a serving, five times the 10 mg adult-use cap, and both stop at 200 mg per package.

faq.q: Is medical cannabis cheaper in Michigan?
faq.a: On taxes, yes. Registered patients owe just the 6% sales tax, while adult-use buyers also pay a 10% excise tax, with the sales tax figured on top of it. On $100 of cannabis, that's $106 versus $116.60. Shelf prices are up to each store, and a card has costs of its own: a $40 state fee every two years plus the physician's visit.

faq.q: Can I shop at an adult-use store with a medical card?
faq.a: Yes, if you're 21 or older, but you'll buy as an adult-use customer with your ID, and adult-use taxes apply. Patients buy as patients at licensed provisioning centers, where they present a registry card and photo ID. High Society welcomes patients 18 and older who carry a valid card, so ask your store how medical purchases work there.

faq.q: If I'm over 21, do I still need a medical card?
faq.a: No. Any adult 21 or older can buy adult-use cannabis with a valid photo ID. A card can still make sense if a physician certifies you for the program and you buy often, since registered patients skip the 10% excise tax. The higher medical limits on infused products are another difference. Your physician can tell you whether you qualify.
